title: Almondz Global Securities Ltd - 531400 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: Almondz Global Securities Q2 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 17.9% YoY to INR40.09 crore, with profit up 2.4x to INR9.13 crore.
summary.overview: Management reported consolidated revenue of INR40.09 crore (up 17.9% YoY) and profit of INR9.13 crore (2.4x), with margin at 22.8%. Premier Green (green fuel JV, 41% stake) drove growth, with Himachal running at 285 KLPD and Odisha plant fully operational. Infra consulting revenue rose 21.1% to INR31.35 crore, while financial services revenue grew 2.7% to INR8.05 crore but profit fell on weak capital markets and lower mark-to-market gains. Management is pursuing a demerger of the infra consulting business, with a second demerger of Premier Green planned afterwards.

segments.name: Infra engineering consulting (Almondz Global Infra Consulting)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR31.35 crore (+21.1%) and profit INR2.90 crore (+19.8%) on higher DPR revenue. H1 order inflow INR154 crore, versus INR72 crore in H1 last year; total order book above INR400 crore to execute over 3-4 years.

segments.name: Green fuel (Premier Green Innovations, 41% stake)
segments.commentary: Himachal unit ran at full 285 KLPD; quarterly revenue INR202.24 crore and profit INR12.59 crore. Odisha 200 KLPD plant is operational and produced 71 lakh litres in its initial phase; full OMC supply expected from third week of November.

segments.name: Financial services (broking, merchant banking, investment banking, wealth)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR8.05 crore (+2.7%) and profit INR2.51 crore, lower due to weak capital markets and reduced mark-to-market gains from last quarter. Wealth management AUM about INR1,500 crore, concentrated in 20-25 family offices.

guidance_outlook: Premier Green: ~INR1,000 crore revenue expected this year (FY27), versus INR700 crore in FY26; ~INR1,400 crore targeted next year, with ~INR800 crore from Himachal and ~INR600 crore from Odisha.
Premier Green capacity utilisation: targeting 80% in Q3 and 100% in Q4 of the 485 KLPD total capacity; 12.80 crore litres of ethanol allocated from Himachal and Odisha.
Infra consulting: revenue expected about INR160 crore this year (versus INR131 crore last year), with at least 25% growth next year.
Financial services: 20-25% revenue growth expected this year versus INR61 crore last year, with similar growth next year; management expects significant fee growth in Q4 FY27.
Management says all three businesses should grow at least 25% YoY over the next five years and expects to remain confident about H2.
capex_capacity: Premier Green Himachal unit operating at full 285 KLPD capacity.
Premier Green Odisha 200 KLPD greenfield plant fully operational; 71 lakh litres produced in initial phase.
Total Premier Green capacity 485 KLPD; order book fully booked to 100% capacity for next year, per management.

Demerger of infra engineering business: NSE approval expected any time; then SEBI and NCLT filings; completion expected in 6-9 months. Ratio tentative: 666 shares of Almondz Global Infra Consultant for every 10,000 held.
Second demerger of Premier Green proposed after the first; ratio to be set on valuation at that time. Infra business is investing in technology-led automation.
demand_pricing: Infra: largest ever sole bid INR33 crore program management consultancy mandate from Odisha Industrial Infrastructure Development Corporation; DPR for 422 km NaMo Expressway (Odisha); authority engineer role for Itarsi-Nagpur 3rd line (Central Railway); first Uttar Pradesh State Bridge Corporation project; first overseas assignment in Zambia; PPP Centre of Philippines empanelment.
Premier Green: OMC allocations finalised for FY27; orders released by oil marketing companies only the day before the call.

Financial services: pipeline of about 5 private placement mandates being executed, expected to close over the next 2-3 quarters; 4 mandates closed in last 2 years. Recent completed placement for Green Joules; Daalchini transaction in final diligence; 3 other mandates ongoing.
Financial services focus on small-cap growth companies with expected valuations of INR100-500 crore.

qa_highlights.question: What is the demerger timeline and the 5-year growth expectation for each listed business?
qa_highlights.answer: NSE approval expected any time; SEBI and NCLT filings follow, with 6-9 months to listing. Management expects each of the three businesses to grow at least 25% YoY.

qa_highlights.question: How is the capital markets business positioned amid market volatility?
qa_highlights.answer: Management says the private placement pipeline targets small-cap growth companies on five-year advisory relationships; about 4 mandates closed in last 2 years and about 5 in execution. The investment book is split equally between debt and equity; private equity exposure is split equally between listed and unlisted stocks.

qa_highlights.question: How will broking and wealth management be scaled?
qa_highlights.answer: Management says broking and wealth growth comes through the investment banking book; wealth AUM is about INR1,500 crore, mostly from 20-25 family offices, with 25-30% annual AUM addition. Management does not see it as a retail broker. A shareholder requested AUM and new client disclosure; management agreed to implement.

qa_highlights.question: Which company is growing fastest and how will the structure look post-demerger?
qa_highlights.answer: Premier Green is the fastest-growing, with ~INR1,000 crore expected this year. Post-demerger, AGSL keeps a 40% stake in Premier Green, with its profit share added to the bottom line; financial services is expected to grow 25-30% next year.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Avonmore holding structure?
qa_highlights.answer: Avonmore Holdings is an NBFC and promoter company; it owns 51% of AGSL, 40% of Almondz Infra Consultancy and 11% of Premier Green. A 100% subsidiary, Almondz Finance, is being merged into Avonmore, with one licence to be surrendered.

risks_watch: Capital market weakness: financial services profit fell and the pipeline depends on mandate closures over the next 2-3 quarters.
Premier Green execution: the 100% utilisation target for Q4 depends on OMC allocations and the Odisha plant ramp-up.
Demerger execution: NSE/SEBI/NCLT approvals and the 6-9 month timeline; ratio subject to regulatory changes.
Wealth management AUM concentration in about 20-25 family offices.
Management's 25%+ growth claim across all three businesses versus the H1 run-rate of financial services (+2.7% revenue).
summary.management_tone: Confident and promotional on infra, green fuel and demerger value unlocking, with forward targets stated firmly. Cautious and vague on financial services, where profit fell and management points to a future pipeline rather than current numbers.
key_quotes: We are pleased to report a strong second quarter.
This shows the operating leverage now coming through across our businesses.
We are targeting in quarter 3 that our total capacity of 485 KLPD In the quarter 4, not in the quarter 3, because in the quarter 3, we shall be targeting 80%.
I recommend that you should recommend this stock to your investors.

adds.what: Premier Green Odisha 200 KLPD greenfield ethanol plant (operational, initial phase produced 71 lakh litres)

growth.why: Management guides Premier Green FY27 revenue ~INR1,000 crore (vs INR700 crore) and FY28 ~INR1,400 crore, with ethanol utilisation targeted at 80% in Q3 and 100% in Q4 of 485 KLPD; Odisha 200 KLPD plant is operational, and infra consulting guides ~INR160 crore (vs INR131 crore) with at least 25% growth next year, backed by H1 order inflow of INR154 crore and a order book above INR400 crore.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Consolidated margin reported at 22.8% with Premier Green (revenue INR202.24 crore, profit INR12.59 crore) driving profit up 2.4x, but financial services profit fell and the 80%/100% utilisation ramp is not yet proven.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Odisha 200 KLPD plant is operational and total Premier Green capacity is 485 KLPD; the ramp to 80% in Q3 and 100% in Q4 is guided, though it depends on OMC allocations.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Premier Green FY27 revenue guided at ~INR1,000 crore vs INR700 crore in FY26, and infra consulting ~INR160 crore vs INR131 crore with H1 order inflow of INR154 crore vs INR72 crore a year earlier.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management is confident on H2 and says all three businesses will grow at least 25% YoY, but financial services revenue grew only 2.7% in H1.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Financial services profit fell on weak capital markets, and the 25%+ growth claim for that segment sits against +2.7% revenue growth; the Q4 100% utilisation target depends on OMC allocations.

rows.label: Infra order book above INR400 crore
rows.why: H1 order inflow INR154 crore vs INR72 crore last year, and total order book above INR400 crore to execute over 3-4 years, including the INR33 crore Odisha mandate.

rows.label: Infra consulting demerger
rows.why: NSE approval expected any time, then SEBI and NCLT filings; tentative ratio 666 shares per 10,000 held, with listing 6-9 months out.

rows.label: Private placement mandate closures
rows.why: About 5 private placement mandates in execution, with 4 closed in the last 2 years; closures would lift the weak financial services fee line, which grew only 2.7%.

tone.note: Management was confident on infra orders, Premier Green ramp and the demerger, and cautious on financial services where profit fell; analysts pushed on capital markets weakness and how the 25%+ growth claim squares with the H1 run-rate.

oneOffs.what: Premier Green (41% stake, green fuel) revenue up 55.7% to INR202.24 crore with Himachal at full 285 KLPD and Odisha plant ramping; ramp-up stage, not clearly recurring at this rate

quality.why: Consolidated revenue rose 17.9% to INR40.09 crore, with growth led by Premier Green's 55.7% jump and infra consulting's 21.1% rise, while financial services grew only 2.7%; the brief does not give a one-off item for the profit jump (2.4x), so the headline profit growth is not clearly explained by the recurring business.
